tables.comment:
A quote from a source, with the reader's note and tags.

`prefix` and `suffix` are a little of the text on each side of the quote,
a W3C Web Annotation text-quote selector, so the quote can be found on the
page again even when it appears there more than once.

columns.name: tags
columns.comment: Comma-separated, lowercase tags, such as `method,cities`.

tables.comment: A note in a project, written in markdown.
A research question, and everything collected for it.

columns.name: title
columns.comment: The project's name, such as "Urban heat islands".

columns.name: question
columns.comment: The question the project tries to answer.

tables.comment: A page someone read: everything a citation needs.

columns.name: site
columns.comment: The site's name, such as "The Guardian".

columns.name: published
columns.comment: When the page was published, as `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM`, or `YYYY-MM-DD`.

columns.name: accessed_at
columns.comment: When it was first clipped, which citations call the access date.

tables.comment:
One per person. Everything else about them, from their emails to their
sessions, points here; the app's own user table shares its key.

columns.name: disabled_at
columns.comment:
When the account was disabled. A disabled account can't sign in, and
its sessions stop working.

columns.name: locked_until
columns.comment: Until when sign-in is refused, after too many failed attempts.

tables.comment:
A short-lived secret a sign-in method sent or expects, such as an email
code or the second step of signing in. Only its hash is stored, it
expires, and it works once.

columns.name: subject
columns.comment: Who it was issued to, such as an email address.

columns.name: state
columns.comment:
What the ceremony needs to finish, such as a WebAuthn challenge or a
PKCE verifier: sealed with the server's keys and bound to this row.

columns.name: attempts
columns.comment: Failed attempts so far.

tables.comment: An email address an account has proved it receives mail at.

columns.name: address
columns.comment: The address, trimmed and lowercased. Each belongs to one account.

columns.name: verified_at
columns.comment: When the account last proved it receives mail here.

columns.name: is_primary
columns.comment: Whether this is the address the account's mail goes to.

tables.comment:
The audit trail: what happened to an account, and from where. Never
credentials.

columns.name: detail
columns.comment:
What it concerns, such as the app that was connected: never a
credential.

tables.comment:
A third-party account someone signs in with, such as their Google
account. Who they are there is the provider and the provider's subject,
never the email address, which some providers let people change to
anything.

columns.name: provider
columns.comment: The provider's ID in `[auth.providers]`, such as `google`.

columns.name: subject
columns.comment: The provider's stable ID for the person.

columns.name: email
columns.comment: The address the provider gave, as it gave it.

columns.name: email_verified
columns.comment:
Whether the provider vouched for that address. Even then, it never
connects accounts by itself.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: Their name or username there, to tell connected accounts apart.

columns.name: last_used_at
columns.comment: When it last signed in.

tables.comment:
An account that was merged into another. Old references to it, such as
profile links, resolve to the account that absorbed it.

columns.name: absorbed_id
columns.comment: The account that no longer exists.

columns.name: survivor_id
columns.comment: The account it became part of.

tables.comment:
A passkey: a key pair on the person's device, or synced through their
password manager, whose public half signs them in. Only public keys are
stored.

columns.name: credential_id
columns.comment:
The credential ID the device names the key by. Each belongs to one
account.

columns.name: credential
columns.comment:
The public key, its algorithm, and its signature counter, as
`webauthn-rs` keeps them, in JSON.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: What the person calls it, such as "iCloud Keychain".

columns.name: backed_up
columns.comment:
Whether it's synced to other devices, such as through a password
manager, rather than bound to one.

columns.name: last_used_at
columns.comment: When it last signed in or confirmed it's them.

tables.comment:
An account's password, as an Argon2id hash in the PHC string format,
which names its parameters, so a hash made with older ones is replaced
at the next sign-in. Nobody reads it but this crate.

columns.name: account_id
columns.comment: One password per account.

columns.name: changed_at
columns.comment: When it was last set, changed, or reset.

tables.comment:
A provider's access and refresh tokens for one connected account, kept
only for providers the app configured with `store_tokens`, so the app
can call that provider's API for the person. Both are encrypted with the
server's keys and bound to the identity, so a copy of the database calls
no one's API. Nobody reads them directly, not even their owner: the app
asks [`Auth::provider_access_token`](crate::Auth), which refreshes them.
Disconnecting the account, merging it away, or deleting the account
deletes them, and revokes them where the provider allows.

columns.name: identity_id
columns.comment: The connected account they belong to: one set each.

columns.name: provider
columns.comment: The provider's ID in `[auth.providers]`, such as `github`.

columns.name: access_token
columns.comment: The access token, AES-256-GCM-SIV under the newest key.

columns.name: refresh_token
columns.comment: The refresh token, sealed the same way, when the provider gave one.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.comment: When the access token stops working, if the provider said.

columns.name: scope
columns.comment: The scopes the provider granted, as it listed them.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.comment: When they were last replaced, at sign-in or by a refresh.

tables.comment:
A fixed-window counter for one action from one source, such as code
requests for one address. The key is a hash, so the table holds no
addresses.

One of an account's recovery codes, for when its authenticator is lost.
Each works once; only its keyed hash is stored.

A signed-in device. The tokens that prove it live only on the device:
this row keeps their SHA-256 hashes, so a copy of the database signs no
one in.

A browser holds one token, in a cookie. A native app holds two: a
short-lived access token it sends with each request, and a refresh token
that trades for a new pair and works once.

columns.name: token_hash
columns.comment: The cookie's token, or a native app's access token.

columns.name: access_expires_at
columns.comment:
When a native app's access token stops working, so it must refresh.
`None` for a browser's cookie.

columns.name: refresh_hash
columns.comment: A native app's refresh token.

columns.name: previous_refresh_hash
columns.comment:
The refresh token this one replaced. Seen again after a short grace,
it means someone else has a copy, and the session ends.

columns.name: refreshed_at
columns.comment: When the refresh token was last replaced.

columns.name: authenticated_at
columns.comment:
When its owner last proved who they are, which carries over when the
session's token is replaced.

columns.name: mfa_at
columns.comment: When its owner last completed a second factor.

columns.name: last_seen_at
columns.comment: When the session was last used, to the minute.

columns.name: idle_expires_at
columns.comment: When it ends unless it's used before then.

columns.name: expires_at
columns.comment: When it ends however often it's used.

columns.name: device
columns.comment: What signed in, such as "Firefox on macOS", for the list of devices.

columns.name: revoked_at
columns.comment: When it was signed out or revoked.

tables.comment:
An account's authenticator app: the TOTP secret it shares with the
server. The secret is encrypted with the server's keys, so a copy of the
database can't produce codes, and bound to its account.

columns.name: account_id
columns.comment: One authenticator per account.

columns.name: secret
columns.comment: AES-256-GCM-SIV under the newest key, with the key's ID.

columns.name: confirmed_at
columns.comment:
When a code from the app first matched. Until then the app isn't
trusted to sign in with.

columns.name: last_used_step
columns.comment: The last 30-second step whose code was used, so no code works twice.

tables.comment:
A wallet linked to an account, with proof that the account's owner
controls it: a Sign-In With Solana message signed by its key. A wallet
belongs to one account. It's private unless its owner shows it, and
signs in only when its owner turns that on.

columns.name: chain
columns.comment: The chain: `solana`.

columns.name: address
columns.comment: The address.

columns.name: label
columns.comment: What the person calls it, such as "Treasury".

columns.name: can_sign_in
columns.comment:
Whether it may sign in to the account. Off until its owner turns it
on.

columns.name: is_public
columns.comment: Whether it shows on its owner's public profile.

columns.name: verified_at
columns.comment: When it was linked.

columns.name: last_proved_at
columns.comment: When it last signed a proof.

columns.name: proof
columns.comment: The latest signed message, kept for audit.

columns.name: proof_signature
columns.comment: The message's signature.

tables.comment: `live.changes`: one row per written row of a live table.

columns.name: seq
columns.comment: The change's place among the database's changes.

columns.name: txid
columns.comment: The Postgres transaction that wrote it, which joins it to its commit.

columns.name: version
columns.comment: SQLite: the commit's version, set just before the commit.

columns.name: table_name
columns.comment: The changed table, with its namespace: `messages` or `billing.invoices`.

columns.name: op
columns.comment: What the write did.

columns.name: key
columns.comment: The changed row's key, in key column order.

columns.name: old
columns.comment:
The row before an update or delete, without `secret` and
`live = skip` columns.

columns.name: new
columns.comment: The row after an insert or update, without those columns.

columns.name: changed
columns.comment: For an update, every column whose value changed; empty otherwise.

tables.comment:
`live.commits`: one row per committed transaction that wrote a live
table.

columns.name: version
columns.comment:
The transaction's place in the version line. Gaps are transactions
that rolled back after taking a version, which never become visible.

columns.name: txid
columns.comment:
The Postgres transaction ID, which joins the commit to its changes.
`None` on SQLite.

columns.name: committed_at
columns.comment: When the transaction committed.

columns.name: actor
columns.comment: Who made the change, when the transaction said.

columns.name: origin
columns.comment:
What made it: what the transaction said, such as an operation's
name, or `sql`.

columns.name: lsn
columns.comment:
Replication capture: where the commit's record starts in Postgres's
write-ahead log, which orders commits as the database committed them.
`None` for commits captured by triggers.
